current_architecture: Canonical project root already exists and is broadly consumed.
why: It is already the correct project anchor and does not create duplicate authority.

current_architecture: Governance already models tenant, company, division, department, region, authority levels, and org nodes, but downstream propagation is incomplete.
why: BR2 overstated absence; the architecture exists in governance and should be propagated rather than replaced.

current_architecture: Canonical roster and role assignment owner already exists.
why: It already serves the right ownership purpose without obvious duplication.

current_architecture: Reusable enterprise cost-code definition owner already exists.
why: A second registry would only weaken source-of-truth discipline.

current_architecture: Project planning is already persisted on jobs_master.assigned_cost_codes and feeds downstream schedule/progress logic.
why: The right architecture already exists; it needs refinement, not relocation.

current_architecture: A deterministic, explainable project schedule engine already exists.
why: Rebuilding would destroy working value without solving the real gaps.

current_architecture: Planning lifecycle already exists on the same project-controls spine.
why: The architecture is already coherent enough to extend rather than split out.

current_architecture: Forecast lineage and overrides already live on the canonical schedule path.
why: This should remain inside the existing schedule/planning spine.

current_architecture: Operational review cadence already exists and is connected to project-controls truth.
why: The concept is right; only bounded refinement is warranted.

current_architecture: Daily Reports are the primary field-entry spine for labor, materials, equipment, and cost-code quantities.
why: Field capture value is already proven; only production fact-boundaries need tightening.

current_architecture: Weekly labor reconciliation lane already exists and is distinct from field capture.
why: It is already useful and bounded; replacing it would add churn, not value.

current_architecture: Daily field constraints and standing blocker workflows both exist.
why: The architecture needs formal connection rules, not a new subsystem.

current_architecture: Demand, roster, and deployment exist across planning, team assignments, and dispatch.
why: The value is real, but semantics are split across systems and should be tightened.

current_architecture: Asset Spine is a strong permanent registry core, with provider-local seams still around it.
why: The right core exists; remaining work is edge normalization, not architectural replacement.

current_architecture: Project Health is an explicitly derived friction/attention surface.
why: It is valuable as a derived view as long as it stays read-side and bounded.

current_architecture: ODS is a real additive read model but overlaps with other executive readers and still carries fixed-tenant assumptions.
why: This is the clearest place to simplify architecture without disturbing upstream truth owners.

current_architecture: Company KPI aggregation exists and is explicitly no-cost/no-budget.
why: The pattern is useful and should remain, but enterprise scope propagation must improve.

current_architecture: A parallel digest/intelligence lane still exists beside newer reporting surfaces.
why: Retaining it increases overlap more than it preserves unique value.

current_architecture: Bounded AI capability already exists for configuration, translation, and briefing generation.
why: AI should remain assistive and downstream of canonical truth, not be expanded as an owner.

current_architecture: Governed permissions, approval flows, separation rules, and audit surfaces already exist.
why: This is one of the most valuable existing architectural assets and should be preserved.

current_architecture: Admin, PM, shop, HR, safety, dispatch, field leadership, and executive routes already exist in one application shell.
why: The platform already supports real role-specific operating surfaces; hierarchy should be tightened, not rebuilt.

current_architecture: A live job-cost snapshot already exists from daily reports, labor-rate input, and materials.
why: It is useful and preservable, but must stay clearly bounded as a live snapshot rather than a budget owner.

current_architecture: PO requests already track estimated amounts, approved amounts, issue/receipt state, and project linkage.
why: It is a strong procurement-adjacent control and should feed, not become, budget authority.

current_architecture: No canonical budget baseline or controller-grade budget owner was evidenced.
why: This layer is genuinely missing, but it should be built on preserved upstream architecture.

current_architecture: No canonical EV owner, formulas, or rollup layer was evidenced.
why: This is still net-new, but only as a derived layer after budget exists.
